Let $\Gamma>0$, real $\omega$, and $b$ real. The Langreth rules for $C = AB$ give the following.
\begin{equation}\label{k1}
\int_0^{\infty} dt\, e^{-t^2} = \frac{\sqrt{\pi}}{2}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}\label{k3}
\int_0^{1} dx\, e^{x^2} = 1.4626517459
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}\label{k5}
\int_{-\infty}^{\infty} dx\, e^{-x^2 + b x} = \sqrt{\pi} e^{b^2/4}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}\label{k6}
C^{<} = A^{<}B^{a} + A^{r}B^{<} +
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}\label{k7}
G = 1, \qquad \Gamma \equiv
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}\label{k8}
C^{<} = (A^{r} + A^{<})(B^{<})
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}\label{k10}
\int_0^{\infty} dt\, e^{-(\Gamma + i\omega) t} = \frac{1}{\Gamma + i\omega}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}\label{k11}
\int_0^{\infty} dt\, \cos(\omega t) e^{-\Gamma t} = \frac{\Gamma}{\Gamma^2+\omega^2}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}\label{k12}
\int_{0}^{\pi} d\theta\, \sin^2\theta = \frac{\pi}{2}
\end{equation}
\begin{equation}\label{k13}
\int_{-\infty}^{0} dt\, t\, e^{\Gamma t} = -\frac{1}{\Gamma^2}
\end{equation}
